target_customer: K-8 teachers who use it free; schools and families, with parents paying for premium features
problem: Teachers named classroom behavior as their biggest problem in hundreds of interviews, and had no light tool to track and encourage it or to reach parents.
business_model: Free teacher app with consumer subscriptions for families and some school products
product_category: Classroom communication and behavior management app

founders.name: Sam Chaudhary
founders.background_notes: Both founders were in the inaugural class of the ImagineK12 education accelerator per TNW in 2012.

technical_complexity.rationale: Web and mobile app with points, reports and messaging; the difficulty was adoption in classrooms rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Each classroom connects teacher, children and parents, which spreads by word of mouth and makes switching mid-year costly; the features themselves were easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; ClassDojo stayed independent, raised a Series C in 2019 and reports 51 million monthly users on its YC page.

market_need_then: Teacher interviews showed behavior management as the top pain, and the free tool reached 3.5 million teachers and students in over 30 countries at its August 2012 launch.

identity.logo: Green monster Mojo on a blue circle per logo archives
identity.mascot_or_character: Mojo the green monster and a set of student monster avatars
identity.voice_and_tone: Cheerful and encouraging, with mission stated as an education children love

branding.community_and_virality: Teachers share Mojo plush toys, and a 2025 Monster of the Year contest drew over 40,000 entries.

brand_strength.rationale: Mascot-led brand with plush merch, annual contests and growth mostly through word of mouth per the YC page.

outcome_analysis: ClassDojo gave teachers a free tool that spread classroom by classroom, raised a seed in 2012 and a 35 million dollar Series C in 2019, and per TechCrunch reached first profits in 2021 after about eight years. It remains private and active, aided by a strong mascot-led brand.
notes: The press release states 65M raised total to 2019, implying about 30M before the Series C beyond the seed, so Series A and B are missing; they were not found. A Series C-II near 30M in January 2021 and a 2022 round with 113.5M and a 1.3B valuation appear only in aggregator search summaries and are unverified, so they are not recorded. ClassDojo's own site returned no founder or name origin. Only 2014 competitor sources (Edmodo, Remind) were found, too late for the batch, so the list is empty.
